correctness.rationale: For vertices in the same part, equal open neighborhoods force at most one omission. For omitted vertices in distinct parts, the traces S\V_i and S\V_j are equal exactly when both corresponding parts are empty in S, which under the first condition occurs exactly for two omitted singleton parts. Total domination is equivalent to S meeting at least two parts. These equivalences prove the classification, and independent multiplication of admissible omission choices gives the polynomial. Exhaustive replay checks every complete multipartite type through order 9.

value.rationale: Complete multipartite graphs are a standard extremal/test family for domination parameters. The result gives an exact all-set classification, a factored polynomial for every part-size profile, the minimum number, and the number of minimum sets, while cleanly identifying the singleton exceptions. This is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
